correctness.rationale: A(n)<=n follows for deficient n from divisorwise monotonicity of sigma(d)/d and the recursive definition. Euler-factor bounds confine all odd three-prime candidates to 3*5*r with r=7,11,13; at most two primes are always deficient. The formal coefficient identity 1/[2(1-X)(1-Y)(1-Z)-1] yields the exact seven-neighbor recurrence. The packaged verify.py enumerates all 11827 exponent triples with product at most N=801204488268064453125 and checks the unique ample triple (20,9,6), independently cross-checking every proper divisor on its box and ordered factorizations. Computations were run from the actual new artifact path with all assertions passed.

value.rationale: Three is the least possible distinct-prime support size for odd ample integers. Identifying the exact least at this first natural layer resolves an effective extremal problem the published infinite-existence theorem explicitly does not settle. The proof combines a structural divisor-sum reduction and complete, reasonably small, independently cross-checked integer certificate; the 21-digit extremal value is not an arbitrary slice and can serve as a canonical benchmark for recursive-divisor searches.
